parsed.answer: This has been reported before (PowerToys#30646): the installer says PowerToys is already installed even though it was removed or the uninstall was botched. The leftover Windows Installer registration is what blocks the setup. A commenter there got unstuck by running the Microsoft Program Install and Uninstall troubleshooter (the link is in that ticket). It listed the stale PowerToys entries, and after uninstalling each one (running it twice if two are listed) and rebooting, a fresh install worked. If Control Panel still lists PowerToys after the reboot, uninstall it again there, reboot once more, then run the installer (per-user or machine-wide). Another commenter on that ticket reported that deleting registry keys and a cleanup tool did not help, so the troubleshooter is the route to try first. As for the bug report ZIP: it is generated from within PowerToys Settings (General > Bug report tool), which isn't available while PowerToys won't install, so attach the installer log instead.
